title: Faithful Tate action detects prime-power divisibility
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $A,B$ be abelian varieties over $k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], and let $\ell$ be a prime different from $\operatorname{char}k$. Use the geometric Tate modules $T_\ell A,T_\ell B$ of [sk-def-av-tate], with coefficient ring $\mathbf Z_\ell$ [def-weil-l-adic-numbers]. Put $M=\operatorname{Hom}_k(A,B)$, the group-scheme homomorphisms [def-sc-group-scheme] with pointwise addition, and $H=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathbf Z_\ell}(T_\ell A,T_\ell B)$. The Tate modules are finite free of ranks $2\dim A$ and $2\dim B$, so $H\cong\mathbf Z_\ell^{4\dim A\dim B}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module]. The componentwise action $\iota:M\to H$, $f\mapsto T_\ell f$, is an injective homomorphism of abelian groups. For every $f\in M$ and integer $n\geq1$, if $\iota(f)\in\ell^nH$, then there is $g\in M$ with $f=\ell^n g$.

source.place: Chapter I, Remark 7.3, printed p.34; Proposition 10.5 and Lemma 10.6, printed p.45; Lemma 10.16, printed p.49 (over the original field k).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-av-commutative], pointwise addition and inverse make $M$ an abelian group: sums of homomorphisms preserve addition because the target group law commutes. Define $\iota(f)(t)_r=f(t_r)$ using the compatible sequences in [sk-def-av-tate, def-tate-module-abelian-group]. Compatibility follows from $f(\ell x)=\ell f(x)$. For $c\in\mathbf Z_\ell$ its residue $c_r$ acts on level $r$, and $f(c_rt_r)=c_rf(t_r)$; hence this map is $\mathbf Z_\ell$-linear. The identities $(f+g)(t_r)=f(t_r)+g(t_r)$ prove that $\iota$ is an additive homomorphism.

source.place: Chapter I, Remark 7.3, p.34, and the componentwise functor immediately after Proposition 10.5, p.45.

proof.text: Choose an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $k$ [def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By [lem-sfb-abelian-field-extension], $A_\Omega$ and $B_\Omega$ are abelian varieties of the same dimensions as $A,B$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-base-change] identifies their $\Omega$-points with the original geometric points, respects addition and multiplication by $\ell$, and therefore identifies their Tate modules and componentwise maps with those in the statement. Apply [prop-av-tate-rank] over $\Omega$. In the resulting finite bases a linear map is uniquely its matrix, with $2\dim B$ rows and $2\dim A$ columns. Listing its entries gives $H\cong\mathbf Z_\ell^{4\dim A\dim B}$. An empty row or column set gives the zero module, as required.

source.place: Chapter I, Remark 7.3, p.34, and Proposition 10.5, p.45; extension and dimension as in Stacks 0BFB and 02FY.

proof.text: For any abelian variety $D/\Omega$, the coordinate projection $T_\ell D\to D[\ell^r](\Omega)$ is surjective. Given $x$ in that finite level, use [lem-sc-isogeny-surjective] repeatedly to choose $x_{r+1},x_{r+2},\ldots$ with $\ell x_{j+1}=x_j$ and $x_r=x$. Each $x_j$ is killed by $\ell^j$ by induction. For $j<r$ put $x_j=\ell^{r-j}x$. This is precisely a compatible sequence in [sk-def-av-tate]. Thus if $T_\ell f=0$, its coordinate formula in step 1 gives $f_\Omega(x)=0$ for every prime-power torsion point of $A_\Omega$.

source.place: Chapter I, Remark 7.3, p.34; the first inference in Lemma 10.6, p.45, expanded using surjectivity of multiplication.

proof.text:
Assume $T_\ell f=0$. Use [lem-sfb-simple-isogeny-decomposition] over $\Omega$ to choose an isogeny $u:\prod_i C_i	o A_\Omega$ with positive-dimensional simple factors. Each restriction $h_i:C_i	o B_\Omega$ of $f_\Omega u$ kills $C_i[\ell^r](\Omega)$ for every $r$, since homomorphisms send torsion to torsion. Suppose $h_i
e0$. Its kernel $H=\ker h_i=C_i	imes_{B_\Omega,h_i,e}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$ is a closed subgroup scheme of $C_i$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. By [lem-sfb-abelian-closed-subgroup-reduced-component], $D=(H_{\mathrm{red}})^0$ is an abelian subvariety of $C_i$ with $\dim D=\dim H$, so simplicity gives $\dim D\in\{0,\dim C_i\}$. If $\dim D=\dim C_i$, then $D=C_i$ as sets: $C_i$ is irreducible by [lem-sc-abelian-variety-characterization], and a longest chain of irreducible closed subsets of $D\subsetneq C_i$ would extend by $C_i$. As $C_i$ is reduced (smooth), the closed subscheme $H$ with full support is $C_i$, so $h_i$ factors through $e$, i.e. $h_i=0$, a contradiction. Hence $\dim D=0$, and the same node gives $H$ finite over $\Omega$, i.e. $H=\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a finite-dimensional $\Omega$-algebra $R$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. Such a scheme has at most $\dim_\Omega R$ distinct $\Omega$-points: for any finite list of distinct evaluations $v_j:R	o\Omega$, choose for each pair $j
e t$ an element distinguishing them; subtract its value at $v_t$ and divide by its nonzero value at $v_j$, then multiply over $t
e j$. The resulting elements $a_j$ satisfy $v_t(a_j)=\delta_{tj}$ and are linearly independent. But [lem-sc-ntorsion-etale] gives $\ell^{2r\dim C_i}$ distinct torsion points in this kernel for every $r$, an unbounded number. This contradiction proves every $h_i=0$. A homomorphism on a finite product is the sum of its restrictions to the factors, since $(c_i)_i=\sum_i\iota_i(c_i)$ on every test scheme. Hence $f_\Omega u=0$, also for the empty product.

source.place: Chapter I, Proposition 10.1, p.42, and proof of Lemma 10.6, p.45; finite-kernel point bound written out by interpolation. Kernel finiteness from the reduced identity component of the kernel (Milne I, discussion after Remark 10.2, p.43).

proof.text: By [lem-sc-isogeny-degree], $u$ is finite and flat; it is surjective by the definition of isogeny [def-sc-isogeny]. It is an fpqc singleton cover: over an affine open its inverse image is affine by finiteness [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and maps onto that open, so it satisfies [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] cancels $u$ in $f_\Omega u=0$ to give $f_\Omega=0$. By [lem-pc-field-extension-fpqc-cover] and [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], $p_A:A_\Omega\to A$ is also an fpqc cover. Cancel it in $f p_A=p_B f_\Omega=0$ by the same descent uniqueness, obtaining $f=0$. Applied to $f-g$ and using step 1, this proves injectivity of $\iota$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.6, p.45; descent of equality by Stacks descent.tex, Tag 023Q (lemma-fpqc-universal-effective-epimorphisms).

proof.text: Now suppose $\iota(f)=\ell^n v$ for $v\in H$ and $n\ge1$. For $x\in A_\Omega[\ell^n](\Omega)$ choose $t\in T_\ell A$ with $t_n=x$ by step 3. The coordinate description of [def-tate-module-abelian-group] gives $f_\Omega(x)=(T_\ell f(t))_n=(\ell^n v(t))_n=\ell^n(v(t))_n=0$. The integer $\ell^n$ is positive and invertible in $\Omega$, so [lem-sfb-abelian-torsion-kernel-divisibility] gives a unique $\Omega$-group homomorphism $b:A_\Omega\to B_\Omega$ with $b q_\Omega=f_\Omega$, where $q=[\ell^n]_A$ [def-sc-mult-n]. This step uses that node only over the algebraically closed field $\Omega$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.16, p.49; Remarks 8.11(f) and 8.12, p.39.

proof.text: The map $q$ over the original field $k$ is finite and flat by [lem-sc-mult-n-finite-flat], and surjective by [lem-sc-mult-n-isogeny]. As in step 5, using the affine-preimage characterization in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], it is therefore an fpqc cover by [def-weil-pbc-fpqc-covering]. Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. The two pullbacks $b_1,b_2:A_S\to B_S$ satisfy $b_1q_S=f_S=b_2q_S$ because $f,q$ are defined over $k$. The map $q_S$ is an fpqc cover by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change], even though $S$ need not be the spectrum of a field or reduced. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent], with target the scheme $B_S$, cancels $q_S$ and gives $b_1=b_2$. Thus $h=p_B b:A_\Omega\to B$ agrees after the two projections $A_S\rightrightarrows A_\Omega$ and is descent data for a morphism into $B$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.16, p.49, over the original field; descent.tex, Tag 023Q, applied to multiplication and to the field-extension cover.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] to the cover $p_A$ and the compatible $h$ of step 7 to get a scheme morphism $g:A\to B$ with $g p_A=h$. It is over $k$: its structure-map equation holds after $p_A$, and descent uniqueness with target $\operatorname{Spec}k$ cancels $p_A$. The fibre-product universal property then identifies the base change of $g$ with $b$. For the group law compare $g m_A$ and $m_B(g\times g)$ on $A\times_k A$ [def-sc-group-scheme]. After the fpqc base change $(A\times_k A)_\Omega\to A\times_k A$ they agree, because $b$ is a group homomorphism; this base change is a cover by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change] and the field cover of step 5. Descent uniqueness gives equality. The unit equation is checked after $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ in the same way. The inverse equation is checked after $p_A$ and cancelled likewise. Thus $g$ is a $k$-group-scheme homomorphism.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.16, p.49; scheme descent in descent.tex, Tag 023Q, with group operations descended by equality detection.

proof.text: The equality $gq=f$ holds after the cover $p_A$, since there it is $bq_\Omega=f_\Omega$, so [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent] gives $gq=f$ over $k$. On every $k$-scheme $T$, the homomorphism law gives $g_T(\ell^n x)=\ell^n g_T(x)$ for $x\in A(T)$, by repeated addition [def-sc-mult-n]. Thus the equality is exactly $f=\ell^n g$ in $M$, proving the divisibility assertion. The construction includes $A=0$ or $B=0$: the associated Tate Hom module is zero, the simple-factor product may be empty, and the only homomorphism is divided by taking $g=0$.

source.place: Chapter I, Lemma 10.16, p.49, and pointwise Hom convention of §10, pp.42–43.
